verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER (the red validator: 4 LEX-01 surface blockers, all fixable by rewording in the unit), 3 MAJOR, 13 MINOR. The unit is well built and lively. Every one of the 99 keys is right. The German is correct on every model surface. du/Sie is right everywhere (Olena–Priya du, neighbours and Hausmeister Sie, Amal Sie until a2.1-u01). The cast agrees with the registries and with u02, u04 and u06, and the scenes have real people in them (Frau Lehmann's fifty years, Olena's lamp, the Hausmeister's note). L2, L1, Sp1, Sp2 and S1 match sd1.json in items, options and bands. The sentence-building items accept every order. The error corrections name what to correct („Korrigieren Sie das Pronomen“). The dictations have no say/de gap, and the typed numbers accept their number words. So most u04 classes stayed closed. Three things stop exit. (1) Both receptive proofs can be solved by string matching; q02 needs no German at all, only „Garten“ plus a number below 700 (the class of u04 r1-F06). (2) The defining half of cd.a1.wohnung-beschreiben (which rooms, which furniture) is never asked of the learner, because the plan's writing task became a personal-data form (the class of u04 r1-F13). (3) The unit's productive verb ziehen occurs only as „ziehen in die/ins …“, a Wechselpräposition with Akkusativ that the spine licenses from a2.1-u02, with no chunk and no detector. Its word-card example adds an adjective ending. The Folge contrasts „in der“ and „in die Kölner Straße“ five lines apart. One u04 class came back: the genitive „die Frage der Partnerin“ (u04 r5-F05 named u05 as due for that edit).

findings.quote: Folge l04 „Die Wohnung ist in der Kölner Straße.“ … l09 „Wir ziehen in die Kölner Straße!“ · ls3-l01 „Guten Tag! Ziehen Sie hier ins Haus?“ · ls3-mo „Sie ziehen in ein Haus in Leipzig. … „Ziehen Sie hier ins Haus? …““ · f3 „Wie viele Leute ziehen in die Wohnung?“ · lx.ziehen productive, example „Priya und Arjun ziehen in eine neue Wohnung.“ · spine g.wechselpraep „Wohin? + Akkusativ, Wo? + Dativ (in die Küche – in der Küche)“ intro a2.1-u02
findings.problem: ziehen is one of the unit's 16 productive lemmas, and every learner-facing instance puts it in the directional „in + Akkusativ“. There are 6 surfaces, one of them the German-only form label that the learner must read to fill f3. The spine licenses that frame only from a2.1-u02, with no chunk before. The word-card example, which is the production model of a productive lemma, adds an adjective ending (g.adj-dekl-unbestimmt a2.1-u04). The Folge sets „in der Kölner Straße“ and „in die Kölner Straße“ five lines apart without a word of explanation. That is exactly the a2.1-u02 contrast, and at the same time the unit teaches „im Wohnzimmer / in der Küche“ as fixed Wo?-phrases and scores that choice in c08. A learner who answers „Wo wohnen Sie?“ by analogy produces ✗„Ich wohne in die Kölner Straße“. GRM-04 has no detector for g.wechselpraep, so no gate can see the class. §9.4 rates a level breach in production models and a gate hole as MAJOR. „Ziehen Sie hier ins Haus?“ is also unidiomatic. A neighbour says „Ziehen Sie hier ein?“ or „Wohnen Sie jetzt hier im Haus?“.
findings.fix: Unit, all words known at u05: ls3-l01 „Guten Tag! Wohnen Sie jetzt hier im Haus?“. ls3-mo situationDe „Sie sind neu in einem Haus in Leipzig. An der Tür steht Frau Lehmann und fragt: „Wohnen Sie jetzt hier im Haus? Und wie ist die Wohnung?““. f3 labelDe „Wie viele Leute wohnen dann in der Wohnung?“, with checklist[2] and modelText to match. Keep Folge l09 as the one instance and gloss it in start.folge.glosses: { token: „ziehen in“, gloss: { en: „move into (in die/ins …)“ } }. Lexicon owner: make lx.ziehen receptive, swapping in e.g. lx.neu (see F11), and give it an example under the ceiling, e.g. „Priya zieht zu Arjun nach Leipzig.“ (zu/nach + Dativ = the u05 chunk; true to casts/series.json). Spine owner: decide whether „ziehen in die/ins …“ gets a chunkFrom a1.1-u05 (a fixed phrase for the moving scene), or whether the frame stays out of A1.1 altogether.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-04: a heuristic det.wechselpraep-richtung placed on g.wechselpraep that matches (ziehen|gehen|kommen|fahren|stellen|legen|hängen|setzen) … (in|an|auf) + (die|den|das|ins|ans|aufs|eine|einen|ein) + NP. Fixtures: hit „Wir ziehen in die Kölner Straße.“ and „Ziehen Sie hier ins Haus?“; miss „Wir wohnen in der Kölner Straße.“ and „Das Sofa steht im Wohnzimmer.“. findings.problem: In German, „mehr als gut“ reads as ‚better than good, excellent‘. The English twin's ‚more than is good‘ does not survive the translation. So the card, and ls1-p11 even more plainly, first gives „zu“ a positive meaning and then contradicts it. That is the sehr/zu confusion that ls1-p02 and c02 train against. The card also teaches „ohne Endung“ while the learner reads „eine eigene Wohnung“ in the Folge and in LS2 with no hint that endings exist before a noun.
findings.fix: Rule-cards owner: „zu heißt: zu viel, das ist nicht gut: Die Wohnung ist zu teuer.“ (en „zu means too much – not good“), which is one word shorter. Optionally add „Vor dem Nomen: eine eigene Wohnung (später).“ within ruleCardMaxWords 60. Unit: ls1-p11 explanation.de „„zu groß“: Das ist nicht gut. Das Sofa ist für das Wohnzimmer zu groß.“

findings.quote: LEX-03 ×4 „Hausmeister (haus+meister) — allocate“ · lx.hausmeister a1.2-u03 productive · „Willkommen im Haus, …“ (dictation source; no lexicon entry in any level) · „Tür“ (t6, L1-02, ls3-mo; no lexicon entry) · lx.stadtteil „Die Wohnung liegt in einem ruhigen Stadtteil.“ · lx.eigen „Ich suche eine eigene Wohnung.“ · lx.nachbar „Frau Lehmann ist unsere Nachbarin.“ · rm03 „Das Wohnzimmer ist groß und hell.“, rm04 „Der Tisch? Er ist neu.“, Sp2 model „Er ist klein, aber sehr schön.“ with lx.neu/lx.schoen/lx.hell receptive
findings.problem: (1) Herr Krause's role noun is introduced here, glossed in LS3 and t6, and it is the key of ls3-i04, an option of ls3-i01 and a tile of ls3-r02. Yet it is allocated to a1.2-u03 (the u04 r5-F03 class: Markt, Prospekt). (2) „willkommen“ occurs 3× and is a dictation word, but no lexicon has it, so the learner must spell an unallocated word from audio. The same holds for „Tür“ across all eight lexicons. (3) Three u05 word-card examples go above the ceiling: a dative adjective ending with the unallocated liegen; suchen (u06) with an ending; unser (g.possessiv-sein-ihr a1.2-u03), and the masculine lemma's card shows the feminine form. LEX-07 reads only exact detectors, and all three hits are heuristic. „eigen“ can be used only attributively; used predicatively it means ‚peculiar‘. So as a lemma it invites ✗„Die Wohnung ist eigen“ in a unit about predicative adjectives. (4) The unit's production chunks (redemittel, Sp2 model) are built on neu, schön and hell, which are receptive, so SRS never schedules their recall (the u04 r4-F02 class).
findings.fix: Lexicon owner: move lx.hausmeister to a1.1-u05 as receptive, allocate lx.willkommen (receptive, u05) and lx.tuer (Goethe-A1 list), swapping out low-yield lemmas (e.g. lx.per, lx.eigen) since newPerUnit is near its top. Rewrite the examples: lx.stadtteil „Der Stadtteil ist ruhig.“, lx.nachbar „Die Nachbarn sind alle sehr lieb.“. Drop lx.eigen and gloss the chunk „eine eigene Wohnung“ (en „a flat of their own“) in the Folge and LS2 glosses. Promote lx.neu, lx.schoen and lx.hell through `promotions`, and demote lx.ziehen (F04) and lx.schreibtisch, which keeps the share near 0.5. Unit, if lx.willkommen is not allocated: change the LS3 dictation source a1.1-u05-ls3-l08 to a1.1-u05-ls3-l09.
findings.proposedRule: LEX-07: run the heuristic detectors on the examples of the unit's own entries too, as advisories, so that examples like lx.stadtteil and lx.eigen surface in the unit's run. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: lx.balkon „plural“: „Balkone“ · LS3 lex.articlePlural source [lx.wohnung, lx.kueche, lx.balkon, lx.nachbar]
findings.problem: Duden lists both „die Balkons“ and „die Balkone“. The schema holds one plural string, so the LS3 article/plural card can accept only „Balkone“. A learner who writes the equally standard „Balkons“ gets at best a TYPO retry and is taught that a correct form is a slip. The generator is not built yet (E1-client.md §4), so the defect is latent, but it is authored now. Once built, it is a defensible second answer that is not accepted.
findings.fix: Unit: replace lx.balkon in the LS3 source with lx.zimmer (die Zimmer) or lx.bad (die Bäder). SCHEMA owner: let `plural` carry variants (e.g. „Balkone|Balkons“) and have the generator accept each.
findings.proposedRule: LEX-07 plus ITM-06: a small registry of German double plurals (Balkon: Balkone/Balkons, Pizza: Pizzas/Pizzen, Komma: Kommas/Kommata, Kaktus: Kakteen/Kaktusse …). An entry on that list must carry all standard plurals, or must not be a lex.articlePlural source. Failing fixture: a1.1-u05 LS3 with lx.balkon. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.problem: Of the 9 advisories, 5 are false positives that every unit will raise. Every title.canDo begins „Sie können“. „Stellen Sie sich vor“ is the lane's own Sp1 instruction (sd1.sp1 instructionsDe „Stellen Sie sich mit Hilfe der Stichwörter vor.“). The two „eigene“ hits are real, but they sit on a conflict between two binding documents. The curriculum plan licenses attributive adjectives receptively at u05, while the spine licenses them only as a chunk from a1.2-u10. The genitive hit is F05, and the remaining canDo reflexive disappears with F01's fix.
findings.fix: Rule-smith: exempt the lane's own instructionsDe wording (sd1.sp1 „Stellen Sie sich … vor“) and a sentence-initial „Sie können“ in title.canDo. Spine owner: either give g.adj-dekl-unbestimmt a receptive chunkFrom a1.1-u05, as the plan says, or keep it at a1.2-u10, in which case the unit glosses „eine eigene Wohnung“ as a chunk (F11). No other unit change.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-04 fixtures at a1.1-u05: „Sie können Ihre Wohnung zeigen.“ in title.canDo and „Stellen Sie sich vor.“ in an sd1.sp1 instructionsDe produce no advisory. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: LS1 [„schon|schön“, „Ofen|Öfen“, „Tochter|Töchter“, „konnte|könnte“] · LS3 focus „ü und u: Stuhl – Stühle, Kuchen – Küche“, source [„Kuchen|Küchen“, „Mutter|Mütter“, „Bruder|Brüder“, „fuhr|für“]
findings.problem: Two of the eight perception pairs do not isolate the vowel they train. In Kuchen [ˈkuːxn̩] and Küchen [ˈkʏçn̩], the length and the ach-/ich-Laut differ as well as u/ü. In Tochter [ˈtɔxtɐ] and Töchter [ˈtœçtɐ], the ach-/ich-Laut differs too. So a learner can pass the pair on the ch sound. „Kuchen – Küche“ in the focus line is the textbook ach/ich pair, not an u/ü minimal pair.
findings.fix: LS1 source [„schon|schön“, „Ofen|Öfen“, „losen|lösen“, „konnte|könnte“]. LS3 focus „ü und u: Stuhl – Stühle, Tour – Tür“, source [„Mutter|Mütter“, „Bruder|Brüder“, „fuhr|für“, „Tour|Tür“]. The readAloud lines stay.

The other unit-side edits are F05–F08 (the ls1-p11 part), F10, F13, F14, F15 and F17, plus the source swaps in F11 and F12. After the unit edits, the expected residue is 3–4 owner-held minors (F11, F12, F16 and F08's card), which is within the limit. u04 r5-F05 (the genitive) had named u05 as due, and it recurred.
